contrary_evidence: Six of seven selected composite PMIs remain above 50, so the evidence indicates regional and sectoral dispersion rather than synchronized global contraction.
Germany's strong flash PMI coexists with a 9.6% year-on-year October fall in steel output and weaker ifo manufacturing confidence; the report explicitly treats the indicators as different measures.
Worldsteel's October global output fell 1.1% year on year, tempering a one-sided expansion narrative even as North America and Africa expanded.
IEA October supply increased by 2.3 million barrels per day and inventories rose, supporting crude rebalancing even while refined-product premiums and shipping constraints remained elevated.
The Chicago Fed NFCI was negative, indicating looser-than-average US conditions; this does not negate the separate IIF estimate of October EM portfolio outflows.
Brazil's central-government primary deficit improved year on year through September, with net revenue and expenditure growth both positive; this tempers a one-sided fiscal deterioration thesis.
Reuters-reported vessel attacks are attributed and do not quantify a sustained physical loss of oil production or exports.
limitations: Flash PMIs are diffusion surveys, not GDP growth rates or official output data.
Worldsteel covers 70 reporting economies representing approximately 98% of 2025 world crude-steel output; steel is a sector measure, not final demand, and US/Russian country figures are estimates.

IIF's US$33.8bn October figure is a monthly non-resident portfolio-flow estimate, not daily November flows, total capital flight or a direct measure of borrowing spreads, FX funding costs or realised investment.
The Chicago Fed NFCI is a broad US-wide composite; it does not describe financing conditions for every borrower or for emerging markets.
The 6.5% real revenue-growth figure in the Brazil fiscal paragraph refers to net revenue after transfers in the Ministry source; the prose uses the shorter term 'revenue'.
Conflict and shipping incidents are attributed to reporting sources or relevant actors; available evidence does not quantify a sustained loss of oil output.

signal_rationale.delta: The 23 November edition examined China's iron-ore/steel chain and exporter inventories. This edition retains a distinct cross-region activity and financing thesis but adds the newly released October global crude-steel data and Germany's November Ifo survey, then updates the market and oil session reported on 24 November. The new evidence shows regional industrial divergence rather than a synchronized collapse.
signal_rationale.evidence: Worldsteel reported 142.4 Mt crude-steel output in October across 70 economies, down 1.1% y/y; Jan-Oct output was down 0.8%. North America rose 5.6%, Africa 7.9%, the EU fell 4.0%, the Middle East fell 27.7%, South America fell 4.1%, and Asia/Oceania was flat. Germany's Ifo climate index rose to 90.6, but manufacturing confidence fell. Reuters reported Nasdaq -1.4%, S&P 500 -0.50%, Dow +0.85%, Brent +2.27% to US$91.40 and a 0.44% dollar decline in its 24 November session report. The Chicago Fed NFCI was -0.478 for the week ending 13 November, the latest observation available before the cutoff, indicating looser-than-average US financial conditions. The IIF's October EM portfolio-flow estimate is a separate monthly measure.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Regional steel production and survey dispersion can shape expectations for orders, employment, inventories and trade; the Chicago Fed NFCI describes broad US conditions while IIF portfolio flows describe non-resident EM allocations. EM outflows may pressure FX liquidity and external refinancing access if persistent, but this edition does not measure the resulting borrowing costs or investment effects. Yields, currencies and energy logistics then influence investment and delivered costs.
signal_rationale.transmission: Regional activity and steel output -> potential changes in orders, employment and inventories -> domestic inflation and monetary policy -> yields and FX. The Chicago Fed NFCI summarizes broad US money, debt and equity conditions and is negative at the cutoff; it is not a direct EM borrowing-cost measure. IIF monthly EM portfolio outflows may pressure FX liquidity and external refinancing access, potentially raising funding costs and restraining investment if persistent; these downstream effects are not directly measured in this edition. Oil supply and shipping reports -> crude and refined-product prices -> transport and industrial costs -> inflation expectations and policy response.
signal_rationale.falsifier: The thesis weakens if subsequent national accounts and industrial-production releases show broad, synchronized acceleration, regional steel-output gaps narrow, the Germany-France survey divergence closes, the Chicago Fed NFCI remains materially negative, non-resident EM portfolio flows return to positive territory and refined-product premiums decline.

key_constraints: Flash PMIs and the Ifo business-climate index are surveys, not GDP growth rates or measured industrial output.

Worldsteel's 70 reporting economies represented about 98% of global crude-steel output in 2025; US and Russian monthly output are estimates. Steel production is not a direct measure of final demand, inventories or trade.
The October steel figures are one month of sector output; year-to-date changes and country-level product mixes differ.
IIF portfolio flows are October monthly estimates, not daily November flows.
The Brazil Ministry of Finance parameter grid was closed on 6 November; it is a forecast vintage, not a realised outcome or market-consensus survey.
FAO's food-price index is an international commodity basket, not a retail-price or household-affordability measure; the latest meat component mixes projected and observed prices and can be revised.
Reports of vessel attacks around the Strait of Hormuz are attributed to Reuters reporting; the available material does not quantify a sustained loss of oil output or exports.
The US Treasury curve and the 24 November Reuters yield observation refer to different dates and should not be merged into a single curve.
The 23 November Brazil Focus medians are market expectations for 2026, not Central Bank forecasts, and are distinct from the Ministry of Finance's 2027 parameter grid.

The Chicago Fed NFCI is a weekly U.S.-wide composite across 105 money-, debt- and equity-market indicators; a negative reading signals looser-than-average U.S. conditions, not the absence of stress for every borrower or in emerging markets. At the 24 November 20:45 BRT cutoff, the latest published value was -0.478 for the week ending 13 November; the next release was scheduled for 25 November.

The IIF October portfolio-flow estimate does not measure emerging-market borrowing spreads, foreign-currency funding costs or realised investment effects; the outflow-to-refinancing channel is conditional, not an observed cost increase.

reproducibility_notes.pmi_comparison: Flash composite PMI output indices published 23–24 Nov 2026; 50 is the expansion/contraction threshold. The values are survey diffusion indices, not GDP growth rates.
reproducibility_notes.treasury_curve: US Treasury official daily par curve, 23 Nov 2026: 2-year 4.63%; 10-year 4.92%; 30-year 5.29%.
reproducibility_notes.brazil_forecast: Brazil Ministry of Finance November 2026 Macrofiscal Bulletin, summary p.3 and detailed grid discussion p.19; grid closed 6 Nov. For 2027, GDP 1.8% (September 2.3%), IPCA 4.5% (3.8%), accumulated Selic 12.93% (12.67%), average exchange rate R$5.34/US$ (R$5.23), and average Brent US$95.20/bbl (US$79.50). The grid's Selic is an accumulated parameter derived from the real rate implicit in the Focus median and converted to nominal terms with the SPE inflation projection; it is distinct from the Focus terminal Selic median of 13.00% at end-2027 in the 19 November report (12.75% one week earlier; 11.75% four weeks earlier). FX and Brent are annual averages, not terminal or spot prices.
reproducibility_notes.oil_market: Reuters settlement values for 23 Nov; IEA November report supplies October production and inventory estimates. Spot/futures settlement and monthly supply estimates are different observation types.
reproducibility_notes.food_prices: FAO October 2026 FFPI: 133.9, down 1.2% m/m; cereal 116.8, down 4.5%; sugar 121.3, up 6.6%.
reproducibility_notes.market_flows: IIF tracker published 5 Nov, estimating October non-resident EM portfolio outflows of US$33.8bn; monthly estimate, not daily flow. The IIF estimate does not measure EM borrowing spreads, foreign-currency funding costs or realised investment effects; those downstream links are conditional mechanisms, not observed outcomes in this report.
reproducibility_notes.brazil_focus: Banco Central do Brasil Focus report with reference date 19 Nov 2026, summarized by B3 on 23 Nov: 2026 GDP 1.70% (from 1.72%), IPCA 5.15% (from 5.11%), and year-end USD/BRL 5.55 (from 5.40). The 2027 terminal Selic median is 13.00% today, compared with 12.75% one week earlier and 11.75% four weeks earlier. These are market medians, not Central Bank forecasts, and are distinct from the Ministry of Finance's accumulated 2027 Selic parameter. Primary PDF: https://www.bcb.gov.br/content/focus/focus/R20261119.pdf.

Production for 70 reporting countries was 142.4 Mt (-1.1% y/y); Jan-Oct was 1,509.3 Mt (-0.8%). October regional changes: Africa +7.9%, Asia/Oceania 0.0%, EU -4.0%, Europe other +5.1%, Middle East -27.7%, North America +5.6%, Russia/CIS/Ukraine -6.8%, South America -4.1%. reproducibility_notes.reuters_markets_24nov: Reuters report dated 24 Nov 2026: Nasdaq -1.4%, S&P 500 -0.50%, Dow +0.85%; Nvidia shares >6% lower after prior session's +31.5%; dollar -0.44%; US 10-year yield 4.928% vs 4.92% late Monday; Brent January futures settled US$91.40/bbl, +US$2.03 or 2.27%, amid reported vessel attacks around Hormuz. reproducibility_notes.financial_conditions: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago National Financial Conditions Index: the 18 November 2026 release reported -0.478 for the week ending 13 November. Negative readings historically indicate looser-than-average US financial conditions. The index aggregates 105 indicators across money, debt and equity markets and traditional/shadow banking. Chicago Fed's release calendar showed the next update scheduled for 25 November (week ending 20 November), after this edition's 24 November 20:45 BRT cutoff. This broad US composite is not a corporate high-yield spread and does not describe emerging-market financing conditions. The negative US NFCI reading is kept separate from EM portfolio outflows and is not used as a direct measure of EM borrower funding costs.
